блок: вход в участок A: block: entry to the A site
<b>Рибосома бактерии 70S</b> (Thermus th: Bacterial 70S ribosome (Thermus thermophilus, PDB 1VY4): the small 30S subunit (yellow — 16S rRNA, orange — proteins) and the large 50S subunit (light blue 23S and 5S rRNA, blue proteins). The pink strand is mRNA; the green, purple and gray ones are tRNAs in the A, P and E sites. Many antibiotics bind right here: bacterial ribosomes (70S) differ from ours (80S), so the drug hits the microbe. The antibiotic molecules are enlarged about threefold.
<b>Элонгация</b> — повторяющийся цикл. 1: Elongation is a repeating cycle. 1) EF-Tu·GTP (turquoise) delivers an aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site, and its anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon. 2) In the peptidyl transferase center (it is rRNA — a ribozyme) the growing chain is transferred onto the new amino acid. 3) EF-G (orange) uses GTP to move the ribosome along by one codon: the tRNAs shift A → P → E. 4) The empty tRNA leaves from E. The chain exits through the tunnel of the large subunit. Switch on an antibiotic to see which step it breaks.
<b>Устойчивость к антибиотикам.</b> В ог: Antibiotic resistance. A huge colony almost always contains rare mutants that tolerate the drug better (orange; green ones are susceptible). The drug quickly kills the susceptible bacteria — after 2–3 days so few are left that the patient already feels better. If treatment of a serious infection is stopped on one’s own, the surviving bacteria multiply again — and many times more of them are resistant. Choose a scenario and click “Run”.
<b>Тетрациклины</b> (тетрациклин, доксиц: Tetracyclines (tetracycline, doxycycline) bind to the small 30S subunit next to the A site and keep aminoacyl-tRNA out of it, so the chain stops growing. They are bacteriostatic and broad-spectrum (chlamydiae, mycoplasmas, rickettsiae). They bind calcium and are deposited in growing teeth and bones, so they are avoided in children under 8 and in pregnancy (short courses of doxycycline are acceptable, and for rickettsial infections it is used at any age); milk and antacids reduce absorption, and photosensitivity may occur.
<b>Аминогликозиды</b> (гентамицин, амика: Aminoglycosides (gentamicin, amikacin) bind to the decoding center of the 30S subunit — helix h44 of 16S rRNA at nucleotides A1492–A1493. Checking of the codon–anticodon pair is weakened: the ribosome accepts “near-cognate” tRNAs, and the wrong amino acids are built into proteins; the faulty proteins damage the membrane. They are bactericidal but do not work against anaerobes (they are pumped into the cell by oxygen-dependent transport). They are ototoxic, because mitochondrial ribosomes resemble bacterial ones (especially in carriers of the m.1555A>G mutation), and nephrotoxic, because they accumulate in proximal tubule cells.
<b>Стрептомицин</b> — первый аминогликоз: Streptomycin was the first aminoglycoside (1943) and the first drug against tuberculosis. It binds to the 30S subunit between 16S rRNA and protein S12 and locks the ribosome in an “error-prone” state, so misreading increases. Resistance often arises from a single mutation in the gene for protein S12.
<b>Левомицетин</b> (хлорамфеникол) садит: Chloramphenicol binds in the peptidyl transferase center of the large 50S subunit and keeps the amino acid in the A site from moving into position, so no peptide bond is formed. Linezolid (a reserve drug against resistant staphylococci) binds here too. Chloramphenicol also inhibits mitochondrial ribosomes — hence reversible, dose-dependent bone marrow suppression. Separately and rarely (about 1 in 25,000–40,000), irreversible aplastic anemia occurs that does not depend on the dose. In newborns the liver conjugates the drug poorly with glucuronic acid, causing “gray baby syndrome”. That is why its use is limited.
<b>Макролиды</b> (эритромицин, азитромиц: Macrolides (erythromycin, azithromycin, clarithromycin) bind in the exit tunnel of the 50S subunit, just beyond the peptidyl transferase center. Synthesis starts, but a chain of a few amino acids runs into the antibiotic and the peptidyl-tRNA drops off. They are used in penicillin allergy and for atypical pneumonias. Side effects: QT prolongation, inhibition of liver CYP3A4 (erythromycin and clarithromycin — dangerous drug interactions), diarrhea and cramps (erythromycin stimulates motilin receptors). Resistance comes from methylation of 23S rRNA at the binding site (erm genes).
<b>Тетрациклин</b> (жёлтый) занимает уча: Tetracycline (yellow) occupies the A site: the aminoacyl-tRNA arrives and bounces off. The chain stalls, but the ribosome is not destroyed — when the drug leaves, synthesis resumes (a bacteriostatic effect).
<b>Аминогликозид</b> (голубой) искажает: An aminoglycoside (light blue) distorts the decoding center: the ribosome accepts a “near-cognate” tRNA (orange) carrying the wrong amino acid, and red beads appear in the chain. Proteins are assembled with errors. The error rate here is greatly exaggerated to make the errors visible.
<b>Левомицетин</b> (розовый) сидит в пеп: Chloramphenicol (pink) sits in the peptidyl transferase center: there is a tRNA in the A site, but no peptide bond forms — the center flashes and the cycle goes no further.
<b>Эритромицин</b> (оранжевый) перекрыва: Erythromycin (orange) blocks the tunnel: the first 6–8 amino acids are added, then the chain runs into the drug, the ribosome stalls, and the peptidyl-tRNA with its short peptide drops off — synthesis starts over and gets stuck again.
<b>Курс, назначенный врачом</b> (здесь 7: The course prescribed by the doctor (7 days here). The drug suppresses both the susceptible and the moderately resistant bacteria, and the immune system finishes off the latter — by the end of the course the colony is gone. Course length is matched to the infection; nowadays courses are kept as short as possible, because every extra day of antibiotics selects resistant bacteria in our own flora. So the main rule is to take exactly as much as prescribed and not to take antibiotics “just in case”.
<b>Без лечения.</b> Колония растёт до пр: No treatment. The colony grows up to the limit set by nutrients and the immune system. Many mild infections (especially viral ones — antibiotics do not work on them at all) clear up on their own; more serious bacterial infections do not.
<b>Рецидив.</b> Лечение брошено на 3-й д: Relapse. Treatment was stopped on day 3, when few bacteria were left and the symptoms had eased. The survivors multiplied again, and there are now about 15 times more resistant ones among them than before: the next course of the same drug will work less well. This is how resistant strains are selected step by step — especially when antibiotics are taken “just in case” or for viral infections.
Рибосома бактерий чуть отличается от наш: The bacterial ribosome differs slightly from ours — and that is enough for a small molecule to stop a microbe without harming the person.
\n <div><h2>Как работают антибиотик:
How antibiotics work

Antibiotics hit what bacteria have and humans lack (or have in a different form). Protein synthesis: a 70S ribosome instead of 80S — tetracyclines, aminoglycosides (30S), macrolides, chloramphenicol, linezolid (50S). The peptidoglycan cell wall — β-lactams (penicillins, cephalosporins) and vancomycin. DNA gyrase — fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin). Bacterial RNA polymerase — rifampin. Folate synthesis — sulfonamides and trimethoprim.

Bactericidal and bacteriostatic

Bactericidal drugs kill (β-lactams, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones); bacteriostatic drugs stop growth, and the immune system finishes the job (tetracyclines, macrolides, chloramphenicol).

Resistance mechanisms

  • Enzymes that destroy the drug (β-lactamases, aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes).
  • Target modification (methylation of 23S rRNA — macrolides; mutations in protein S12 — streptomycin).
  • Efflux pumps that expel the drug (tetracyclines) and reduced permeability.
  • Ribosomal protection: the TetM and TetO proteins remove tetracycline from the ribosome.
  • Resistance genes are transferred between bacteria on plasmids.

Antibiotics do not work on viruses: viruses have no ribosomes or cell wall of their own.

Simplifications

  • The ribosome is the real 70S structure (PDB 1VY4): rRNA and proteins are shown as tubes along the backbone; the antibiotic sites are the centers of the corresponding nucleotides from crystal structures of the complexes. The drug molecules are enlarged about threefold.
  • The elongation cycle is a diagram: the subunits are schematic, the tRNA shape is real; speeds and sizes are not to scale.
  • The colony is a simple model of growth, immunity and drug action, not a prognosis for any particular disease; the number of resistant bacteria on screen is exaggerated to make them visible.
  • The error rate with aminoglycosides is exaggerated (in reality it is a fraction of a percent).

ТТГ и свободный T₄: норма — серые полосы: TSH and free T₄: gray bands show the normal range
<b>Фолликул щитовидной железы</b> — пузы: A thyroid follicle is a small sac made of a single layer of thyrocytes, filled with colloid containing the protein thyroglobulin. 1) Iodide from the blood is pumped into the cell by the sodium–iodide symporter (NIS, blue) and passes into the colloid through pendrin (green). 2) Thyroid peroxidase (TPO, orange) oxidizes iodine and attaches it to the tyrosines of thyroglobulin, giving MIT (one iodine) and DIT (two). 3) The same TPO couples DIT + DIT → T₄ (thyroxine) and MIT + DIT → T₃. 4) On the TSH signal the cell takes up a droplet of colloid, lysosomes break down thyroglobulin, and T₄ (≈90%) and T₃ are released into the blood.
<b>Ось гипоталамус — гипофиз — щитовидна: The hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid axis. The hypothalamus releases thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH), which makes the pituitary release thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and TSH makes the thyroid gland produce T₄ and T₃. Thyroid hormones inhibit the hypothalamus and pituitary (red arrows), which keeps their level constant. That is why the key test is TSH: it is the first to sense a shift. In the liver and other tissues T₄ is converted into active T₃. Choose a disease.
<b>Как T₃ действует на клетку.</b> T₄ вх: How T₃ acts on a cell. T₄ enters through the MCT8 transporter (green), and deiodinase D2 (orange) removes one iodine, giving active T₃. It passes into the nucleus and binds the thyroid hormone receptor (TR, yellow), which sits on DNA paired with RXR (light blue). Genes are switched on: more Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase (blue pumps in the membrane), more mitochondria and oxidative enzymes — the cell uses more energy and gives off more heat. T₃ also enhances the effect of epinephrine on the heart and is needed for brain maturation in the fetus and child.
<b>Аутоиммунный тиреоидит Хашимото</b> —: Hashimoto’s autoimmune thyroiditis is the most common cause of hypothyroidism. Lymphocytes destroy the gland, T₄ falls, the feedback weakens, and the pituitary releases more and more TSH — high TSH, low T₄. Metabolism slows down: fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin, swelling, slow pulse, constipation, depression. In newborns, untreated hypothyroidism leads to cretinism, which is why all babies are screened for TSH.
<b>Болезнь Грейвса</b> (диффузный токсич: Graves’ disease (diffuse toxic goiter). The immune system makes antibodies to the TSH receptor (purple) that activate it without any TSH. The gland enlarges and works nonstop, and feedback silences the pituitary — TSH near zero, high T₄. Palpitations, sweating, tremor, weight loss despite a good appetite, irritability; in Graves’ disease also bulging eyes (Graves’ ophthalmopathy).
<b>Нехватка йода</b> — в мире главная пр: Iodine deficiency is the main cause of goiter worldwide. Without iodine there is nothing to make T₄ from; TSH rises and makes the gland grow: endemic goiter. The enlarged gland partly compensates for the shortage. Deficiency is especially dangerous for pregnant women and children, because brain development suffers. Prevention is iodized salt.
<b>Лечение гипотиреоза</b> — таблетки <b: Treatment of hypothyroidism: daily levothyroxine tablets (synthetic T₄) for life. The dose is adjusted by TSH: when it returns to normal, there is enough hormone.
<b>Тиамазол</b> и пропилтиоурацил блокир: Methimazole (thiamazole) and propylthiouracil block thyroid peroxidase — iodine is no longer attached to thyroglobulin, and T₄ falls to normal. Other options are radioactive iodine (the gland takes it up itself and is destroyed) or surgery; the fast pulse is brought down with β-blockers.
<b>Йодированная соль</b> возвращает желе: Iodized salt gives the gland back its raw material: T₄ rises, TSH falls, and the goiter may shrink over months (a large, long-standing goiter no longer will). An adult needs about 150 µg of iodine a day; a pregnant woman, 250 µg.
<b>Тиамазол / пропилтиоурацил</b> блокир: Methimazole / propylthiouracil block thyroid peroxidase: iodine keeps entering the colloid but is not attached to tyrosines, so no new T₄ or T₃ is formed. The hormone stored in the colloid lasts several weeks, which is why treatment does not take effect immediately.
<b>Мало йода в пище</b>: NIS работает вп: Too little iodine in the diet: NIS works at half capacity, tyrosines are iodinated slowly, and more MIT and T₃ are made than T₄. There is not enough hormone, and the pituitary responds by raising TSH (“Axis and diseases” mode).
<b>Мало T₃</b> (гипотиреоз): гены почти: Low T₃ (hypothyroidism): genes are barely switched on, there are fewer pumps and mitochondria, and the basal metabolic rate drops by 30–40% — the person feels cold, sluggish and slow.
<b>Много T₃</b> (тиреотоксикоз): клетки: High T₃ (thyrotoxicosis): cells burn fuel wastefully, a lot of heat is produced, and the metabolic rate rises one and a half to two times; the heart beats faster because T₃ adds β-adrenergic receptors.
Два гормона из аминокислоты тирозина и й: Two hormones made from the amino acid tyrosine and iodine set the metabolic rate of every cell in the body — from the heart to the growing brain.
\n <div><h2>Гормоны щитовидной желе:
Thyroid hormones

T₄ (thyroxine, 3,5,3′,5′-tetraiodothyronine) and T₃ (3,5,3′-triiodothyronine) are iodinated derivatives of tyrosine. The gland secretes mostly T₄; about 80% of T₃ is formed in tissues by deiodinases D1 and D2. Deiodinase D3 produces inactive reverse T₃ (rT₃). In the blood more than 99% of the hormones are bound to proteins (thyroxine-binding globulin, transthyretin, albumin); only the free fraction is active.

Synthesis

  • Iodide uptake: the sodium–iodide symporter (NIS), secondary active transport.
  • Oxidation of iodine and iodination of the tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin — thyroid peroxidase (TPO), which requires H₂O₂.
  • Coupling: DIT + DIT → T₄; MIT + DIT → T₃.
  • Proteolysis of thyroglobulin in lysosomes releases T₄ and T₃; the iodine from MIT and DIT is recycled.

Action

The nuclear receptors TRα and TRβ, paired with RXR, bind to DNA sites (TREs) and change gene transcription. Effects: higher basal metabolic rate and heat production, increased lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, lower cholesterol, growth and maturation of bone and brain, and stronger effects of catecholamines on the heart.

Tests

TSH (normal about 0.4–4.0 mU/L), free T₄ (about 10–22 pmol/L), antibodies to TPO (Hashimoto’s) and to the TSH receptor (Graves’).

Simplifications

  • T₄ and T₃ on the right are molecules built from their chemical formulas; everything else (cells, proteins, transporters) is schematic and not to scale.
  • The DNA in the nucleus is a real B-DNA structure (PDB 1BNA); the TR and RXR receptors are schematic blobs.
  • The axis is a simple feedback model; the TSH and T₄ values are typical, not diagnostic cutoffs.

<b>Кора надпочечников</b> делает стероид: The adrenal cortex makes steroid hormones from cholesterol. The first step is the same everywhere: in the mitochondria CYP11A1 cleaves off the side chain, giving pregnenolone. After that the pathway depends on the zone: the zona glomerulosa makes the mineralocorticoid aldosterone (retains Na⁺ and water), the zona fasciculata the glucocorticoid cortisol, and the zona reticularis androgens (DHEA, androstenedione). Each enzyme adds or removes a single group, which is why the molecules look so alike. Choose a zone.
<b>Клубочковая зона</b> — только здесь е: The zona glomerulosa is the only zone with aldosterone synthase, and it lacks 17α-hydroxylase. It is stimulated by angiotensin II and a rise in blood K⁺ (not by ACTH). Aldosterone makes the kidneys retain Na⁺ and water and excrete K⁺, so blood pressure rises.
<b>Пучковая зона</b> — самая толстая; по: The zona fasciculata is the thickest; under the action of ACTH it makes cortisol: the pathway goes through 17α-hydroxylation, then 21- and 11β-hydroxylases. Cortisol is the hormone of prolonged stress: it raises glucose (gluconeogenesis), breaks down muscle protein, and suppresses inflammation and immunity.
<b>Сетчатая зона</b> — <b>17,20-лиаза</b: In the zona reticularis, 17,20-lyase cleaves off the entire side chain, producing androgens: DHEA and androstenedione. In women this is the main source of androgens; in men most testosterone is made by the testes.
<b>Две системы стресса.</b> Быстрая: сим: Two stress systems. The fast one: within seconds a sympathetic nerve (orange) makes the adrenal medulla release epinephrine — the heart beats faster, the bronchi dilate, the liver releases glucose. The slow one: hypothalamus (CRH) → pituitary (ACTH) → adrenal cortex → cortisol; it builds up over minutes, lasts for hours, and itself inhibits the pituitary (gray arrow). Click “Stress” and watch the graph.
<b>Синдром Кушинга</b> — избыток кортизо: Cushing’s syndrome is an excess of cortisol (a tumor of the adrenal gland or the pituitary, or glucocorticoids taken as medication). High glucose (steroid diabetes), obesity of the face and trunk with thin arms and legs, stretch marks, osteoporosis, hypertension, weakened immunity. With an adrenal tumor, ACTH is suppressed by feedback.
<b>Болезнь Аддисона</b> — разрушение кор: Addison’s disease is destruction of the adrenal cortex (most often autoimmune). There is no cortisol or aldosterone: weakness, low blood pressure, low glucose, salt craving, loss of Na⁺ and a rise in K⁺. Without feedback the pituitary pours out ACTH, and its precursor also yields melanocyte-stimulating hormone, so the skin darkens. An Addisonian crisis is dangerous; treatment is hormone replacement.
<b>Феохромоцитома</b> — опухоль мозговог: Pheochromocytoma is a tumor of the adrenal medulla that releases catecholamines in bursts: sudden palpitations, headache, sweating, blood pressure spikes. Diagnosis: metanephrines in blood and urine; treatment: surgery after α-adrenergic blockade.
<b>Как стероид включает ген.</b> Стероид: How a steroid switches on a gene. Steroids are fat-soluble and cross the membrane on their own. Inside, nuclear receptors await them; shown here is the real ligand-binding domain of the progesterone receptor with progesterone in its pocket (PDB 1A28). The hormone closes the pocket with helix 12 (pink), a coactivator (purple) binds to it, and together they switch on genes on DNA. The receptors for cortisol (GR), aldosterone (MR), androgens and estrogens are built the same way.
<b>Кортизол</b> действует через глюкокор: Cortisol acts through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR), a relative of the one shown. But the mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptor, MR, binds cortisol just as tightly, and there is hundreds of times more cortisol in the blood! In the kidney MR is protected by the enzyme 11β-HSD2, which converts cortisol into inactive cortisone. Glycyrrhizin from licorice blocks this enzyme — cortisol then “switches on” MR, sodium is retained, and blood pressure rises.
<b>Альдостерон</b> через MR в клетках по: Aldosterone, acting through MR in renal tubule cells, switches on the genes for the ENaC sodium channel and Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase: sodium and water return to the blood, and potassium goes into the urine. The MR antagonist spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic and a drug for heart failure.
<b>Мифепристон</b> занимает тот же карма: Mifepristone occupies the same pocket but prevents helix 12 from closing (the pink helix swings away) — the coactivator has nothing to bind to, and the gene stays off. This is how receptor antagonists work: mifepristone blocks the progesterone receptor (and, at high doses, the cortisol receptor) and is used in gynecology; tamoxifen (estrogens) and antiandrogens work on the same principle.
<b>Врождённая гиперплазия коры</b> (дефи: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency, about 1 in 10,000–15,000 newborns). Neither cortisol nor aldosterone can be made: the precursor 17-OH-progesterone accumulates (it is the basis of the diagnosis, including newborn screening) and is diverted into androgens. With little cortisol, the pituitary pours out ACTH and the cortex enlarges. Girls show signs of androgen excess already at birth, and some children have life-threatening salt wasting. Treatment: hydrocortisone and, if needed, fludrocortisone.
<b>Хронический стресс</b>: кортизол пост: Chronic stress: cortisol is constantly elevated — higher blood sugar and blood pressure, poorer sleep, weaker immunity, belly fat builds up, and memory suffers (the hippocampus is rich in cortisol receptors).
Две железы в одной: кора из холестерина: Two glands in one: the cortex makes steroids from cholesterol — aldosterone, cortisol, androgens — while the medulla releases epinephrine within seconds.
\n <div><h2>Стероидные гормоны</h2>:
Steroid hormones

All steroids are cholesterol derivatives with four rings (cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene). The enzymes of steroidogenesis are mostly cytochromes P450 (CYP11A1, CYP17, CYP21, CYP11B1, CYP11B2) in the mitochondria and ER. Cholesterol is carried into the mitochondrion by the StAR protein — this is the rate-limiting step, and ACTH speeds it up via cAMP.

Regulation

  • Aldosterone — the renin–angiotensin system and K⁺.
  • Cortisol — ACTH, the circadian rhythm (peak in the morning), stress; feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary.
  • Medullary catecholamines — sympathetic nerves (acetylcholine); epinephrine synthesis (PNMT) requires cortisol, which reaches the medulla from the cortex through the shared blood supply.

Glucocorticoids as drugs

Prednisolone and dexamethasone suppress inflammation and immunity (phospholipase A₂, cytokines). Long-term use causes Cushing’s syndrome and suppression of the body’s own adrenal cortex, so they are withdrawn gradually.

Simplifications

  • The molecules follow their chemical formulas; the adrenal section and the body are schematic.
  • The receptor is the real ligand-binding domain of the progesterone receptor with progesterone (PDB 1A28); the other molecules are placed in the pocket approximately, and the movement of helix 12 is shown schematically.
  • Hormone levels during stress are a qualitative model.
